Title: The woman in the middle of Nvidia spy scandal
Article:
SINGAPORE-BASED tech group Megaspeed dealt in billions of dollars' worth of the world's most advanced AI chips, and its former director, Alice Huang, was this week outed as an alleged Chinese spy.
She was accused of having an affair with Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang while digging up company secrets for Beijing.
Details about Alice Huang's life are vague, making it almost impossible to pin down where she lives, where she works, or when she was born.
But her influence undoubtedly spreads far and wide, from the nondescript Singapore office, to hulking data centres in Southeast Asia, to the gleaming boardrooms of Silicon Valley.
Her connection to cloud computing firm Megaspeed sits at the centre of the scandal.
Megaspeed touts itself as a company at the heart of the AI revolution, using Nvidia's advanced silicon chips to power high-performance computing inside vast data centres.
But it is also under investigation for serving a murkier purpose.
Megaspeed has allegedly helped Beijing skirt trade restrictions by sending Nvidia chips into China.
Beijing has denied allegations of spying, and Megaspeed said it was investigating if it had complied with export controls on the sensitive chips.
Singapore police opened an investigation in February 2025 into Megaspeed and other companies suspected of circumventing or violating export controls.
Alice Huang was interviewed as part of Singapore's probe. Although no charges were laid, she was barred from the city-state in February 2026 for providing inaccurate information to "down-play her role in Mega-speed".
A company linked to her acquired the Singapore arm of Chinese video game developer 7Road International in early 2023.
The 7Road name was then changed to Megaspeed International.
Huang was listed as a Megaspeed director for less than a year, taking the role between March and November 2023.
Her arrival coincided with a drastic change in fortunes, as Megaspeed pivoted from a little-known video game maker to one of Asia's biggest buyers of Nvidia chips.
Over two years, Megaspeed reportedly traded in upwards of US$4 billion worth of Nvidia chips.
Megaspeed has a Malaysian subsidiary that struck a deal in 2024 pledging assets to Apex Enterprise Solutions in Singapore as security in case of contractual breaches.
In June 2025, US investigators turned up at Megaspeed to carry out a "post-shipment verification", with Huang present, according to Singapore's Home Ministry.
That same day, Huang was interviewed by Singapore police, who impounded her passport.
By then, she and Nvidia boss Jensen Huang had already been spotted together in public.
In one of their early outings together, they were seen mingling at an afterparty following the Computex trade show in Taiwan at the beginning of 2024.
The scandal has sparked national security fears.
China and the United States are fighting for supremacy in artificial intelligence, and Nvidia's market-leading products have become a major point of contention.
Nvidia controls an estimated 90 per cent of the market for the chips used to train and run AI models, and the US imposed rules in 2022 to restrict their sales to China.
In any case, the restrictions appear to have been circumvented.
A Chinese university tied to the nation's defence establishment was able to buy advanced Nvidia chips, according to procurement notices from October and September.
Alice Huang sits in the middle of a corporate web, connected to myriad shell companies, investment houses and major Chinese technology firms.
Corporate records filed in Hong Kong list her as a director of Nanjing Lingxing Technology, which operates the popular T3 ride hailing platform in China.
Other notable investors in Nanjing Lingxing Technology include Alibaba and Tencent, as well as state-backed carmakers like China FAW and Dongfeng Motor Group.
A corporate CV published by a Chinese investment firm details Huang's rapid ascent through the ranks of Asian investment banking.
She served in a senior role at HSBC around 2012, the resume claims, before moving on to stints at CITIC Securities and Shanghai Hexi Investment.
She was born in China's Hunan province, which she left to study media in Hong Kong, HK01 media reported. A CCTV reporter wrote on Weibo that she worked with Huang at the Chinese broadcaster, but later deleted the post.
The writers are from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rauf to be sworn in as Melaka chief minister tomorrow
Article:
MELAKA: State Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh is expected to be sworn in as Melaka Chief Minister tomorrow after BN and Perikatan Nasional secured enough seats to form the state government in the 16th Melaka election.
The swearing-in ceremony is scheduled for 11am at the Melaka Yang di-Pertua Negeri's office, paving the way for Rauf to serve a second term as chief minister.
BN and PN won 24 of the 28 state seats contested, giving the coalition partners a two-thirds majority in the state assembly.
BN won 21 seats, while PN secured three.
Earlier, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced that the two coalitions would nominate Rauf to continue leading the state government
following their victory.
Rauf secured a more comfortable victory in defending the Tanjung Bidara seat, winning by a majority of 8,615 votes, compared with just 364 in the 2021 Melaka election.
He defeated Pakatan Harapan candidate Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri in a straight fight.
In the 2021 election, Rauf won Tanjung Bidara in a three-cornered contest with 3,559 votes, ahead of PN candidate Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin, who secured 3,195 votes, and PH candidate Zainal Hassan, who received 489 votes.
Rauf was appointed the 13th Melaka Chief Minister on March 31, 2023, replacing Datuk Seri Sulaiman Md Ali, who resigned.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NST Leader: White-collar crime invading our homes
Article:
The latest commercial crime figures released by Bukit Aman paint a worrying picture that should concern the police and the public.
Data for January to October this year show a 15.88 per cent increase in arrests and a 52 per cent rise in charges brought.
Despite the increases, losses from commercial crimes rose 30.95 per cent to RM5.25 billion from RM4.01 billion in the corresponding period last year.
More troubling is the 235 per cent surge in losses from e-financial crimes to RM280.72 million from RM83.71 million a year earlier. Police need to examine more closely why increased arrests and prosecutions have yet to translate into lower financial losses for Malaysians.
Have fraudsters and scam syndicates become more sophisticated, inflicting heavier losses on victims despite increased arrests?
If so, tackling commercial crime will require a more comprehensive approach involving intelligence-sharing, international cooperation and closer scrutiny of financial institutions, telecommunications companies and technology platforms.
Efforts to identify the masterminds behind criminal syndicates, trace stolen funds and disrupt the financial networks sustaining their operations must also be stepped up.
More resources must be channelled to intelligence and investigative work to dismantle these criminal networks.
The authorities must stay ahead of these criminals by monitoring financial transactions and tracing how ill-gotten gains move through local and international financial networks before being laundered.
Banks, money-transfer operators, telecommunications companies and foreign law enforcement agencies must work together to close loopholes exploited by operators of mule accounts.
In addition, a public awareness campaign is essential to educate people about the risks of commercial crime and how to avoid falling victim to scams.
Bukit Aman's Commercial Crime Investigation Department director Commissioner Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said the public must not trust calls, messages or offers of investment schemes from unknown individuals over the phone line or through emails.
People should never disclose banking details, passwords, one-time passwords (OTPs) or transaction authorisation codes (TACs) to anyone claiming to represent a bank or other trusted organisation.
While the police can pride themselves on the increases in arrests and prosecutions, the scale of financial losses shows that the battle against scammers and fraud syndicates is far from won.
White-collar crime is no longer confined to boardrooms. It has reached the homes of ordinary Malaysians, making the task of enforcement considerably more challenging.
Complacency is not an option.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PN leaves Melaka exco appointments to Rauf's discretion, says Idris
Article:
MELAKA: Perikatan Nasional is leaving it to Melaka Chief Minister-elect Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh to decide whether its assemblymen should be appointed to the state executive council (exco).
Pas vice-president Datuk Idris Ahmad said he would not comment further on the matter as it fell entirely under Rauf's prerogative.
"That is the Chief Minister-elect's prerogative. I have no comment on this. What matters to us is our agenda today. The first step was to win first," he told reporters after the announcement of the unofficial results for the 16th Melaka state election at the Melaka International Trade Centre.
Idris also described PN candidates' victories over prominent political figures in several key seats as evidence of public support for the Melaka unity wave.
"We have proven that we can be giant-killers, with our candidates defeating prominent opponents, including Ridhuan Syarif," he said.
PN won three state seats in the Melaka election — Paya Rumput, Bemban and Bukit Katil — and will join Barisan Nasional in forming the state government.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man shot dead at diesel depot in Penang
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM: A 41-year-old man was shot dead at an industrial diesel storage depot in Mukim 14, Bukit Minyak.
The incident occurred at 4.30pm, with the victim believed to have been shot three times in the body and leg.
The suspect, believed to be the victim's colleague and also in his 40s, fled the scene immediately after the shooting.
Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim confirmed the incident when contacted.
"The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder," he said.
Under Section 302 of the Penal Code, anyone convicted of murder is punishable by death or imprisonment for between 30 and 40 years.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: DAP rules out leaving PH despite electoral setback
Article:
MELAKA: DAP has ruled out leaving Pakatan Harapan despite being the only component party in the coalition to secure seats in the Melaka election.
State DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong said the party remained committed to PH, adding that relations among its three component parties remained strong despite the disappointing election results.
"We will remain in Pakatan Harapan. Relations among the three component parties remain close.
"We also continue to support Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim as our leader and Prime Minister," he said in a press conference.
Khoo was responding to a question on whether DAP would consider leaving PH following the coalition's poor electoral performance.
DAP successfully defended all four of its state seats, while its coalition partners, PKR and Amanah, failed to win any seats in the state assembly.
The four seats were Kota Laksamana, Kesidang, Ayer Keroh and Bandar Hilir.
Despite retaining all its seats, Khoo acknowledged that PH's overall performance had fallen short of expectations.
He said all component parties must collectively shoulder responsibility for the outcome rather than place the blame on any one party.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: BN-PN's identity politics contributed to PH's setback, says DAP chief
Article:
MELAKA: Melaka DAP chairman Khoo Poay Tiong has attributed Pakatan Harapan's defeat in the state election to identity politics employed by Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional.
He claimed that the two coalitions had used narratives centred on Malay and Muslim unity, making it difficult for PH's other component parties to secure electoral support.
"From what I observed, our component parties came under pressure from BN and PN, which employed a strategy of identity politics.
"They used narratives that Malays must unite and Muslims must unite. I believe these tactics made things difficult for our component parties in this election," he told a press conference.
Khoo said DAP, however, managed to retain all four of its state seats, which he attributed to the continued support of its loyal voters.
He acknowledged that PH's overall performance had fallen short of expectations, particularly as its other component parties failed to secure any seats.
"Although we managed to defend all four of our seats, our component parties were unsuccessful this time.
"This is something we must examine thoroughly through a post-mortem to identify our weaknesses and regain the people's support," he said.
The Kota Melaka member of parliament said the election results had sent a clear message to PH, stressing that all component parties must collectively shoulder responsibility for the outcome.
PH won four of the 24 seats it contested in the Melaka election, namely Kota Laksamana, Kesidang, Ayer Keroh and Bandar Hilir, based on unofficial results.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Macron to make first Malaysia visit since 2017, elevate ties to strategic partnership
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: French President Emmanuel Macron will make an official visit to Malaysia on Nov 16 and 17, marking his first trip to the country since 2017.
The visit is expected to usher in a new chapter in Malaysia-France relations, with both countries set to elevate their longstanding ties to a strategic partnership covering defence and security, critical minerals, the energy transition, aeronautics and space, artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity and semiconductors.
According to the French Presidency, the two countries will develop their cooperation based on common priorities while strengthening collaboration on major regional and international issues, as well as relations between Europe and Asean.
France described Malaysia as a key partner of France and the European Union (EU) within Asean, highlighting Malaysia's chairmanship of the regional bloc in 2025 and both countries' shared commitment to multilateralism and international law.
"France and Malaysia are both committed to multilateralism and compliance with international law, and are working to support peace and stability in Southeast Asia and in the Indo-Pacific," the Presidency said, noting France's distinctive role in the region through its overseas territories.
The French Presidency provided the information in a background briefing ahead of the visit, which was shared with Bernama by the French Embassy in Malaysia on Friday.
The visit builds on the momentum generated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's official visit to France in July 2025, the first by a Malaysian head of government in 15 years.
The French Presidency described Macron's upcoming visit as "a new step" in bilateral relations.
On economic relations, the Presidency said France was Malaysia's 10th-largest economic partner and ranked third among EU member states, with bilateral trade reaching €4.7 billion (about RM21.23 billion) in 2025, an increase of 11 per cent from 2024.
"There is a significant French economic presence, with around 300 subsidiaries of French companies and 300 French-owned businesses under local law, employing some 30,000 people," it said, adding that France was Malaysia's 12th-largest investor and second-largest European investor in 2025.
On critical minerals, the Presidency said cooperation between the two countries was advancing, driven by a shared ambition to diversify and secure strategic supplies by strengthening their respective ecosystems across the value chain.
It cited the industrial partnership between French company Carester and Malaysian firm Malaco Mining, signed in 2025 during Anwar's visit to Paris.
The partnership aims to develop local rare earth element mining and separation capabilities while meeting high environmental and social standards.
In the energy and technology sectors, cooperation includes the energy transition, civil nuclear energy, sustainable aviation fuel and carbon capture projects.
The Presidency also highlighted the complementary strengths of both countries in semiconductors.
"Complementarity between Malaysian capacities in the manufacture and packaging of semiconductors and French expertise in research, design and specialised technologies opens up cooperation possibilities that will help diversify and strengthen the resilience of global supply chains in this key sector," it said.
The last visit by a French president to Malaysia was in March 2017, when then-president Francois Hollande undertook a two-day state visit. The visit coincided with the 60th anniversary of diplomatic relations between the two countries.
Macron's visit to Malaysia will follow his state visit to Cambodia from Nov 14 to 16, where he is expected to focus on strengthening bilateral relations, particularly in economic affairs, culture and healthcare.
He will also attend the 20th Francophonie Summit in Phnom Penh on Nov 15 and 16, bringing together representatives of 90 states and governments under the theme "Reinvest in Peace for Shared Prosperity and Sustainable Stability".
The Cambodia visit will also focus on strengthening cooperation in infrastructure, energy, healthcare, transport, agriculture and heritage preservation, while reaffirming the longstanding relationship between the two countries, which dates back to the 1991 Paris Peace Agreements.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [OFFICIAL] BN wins 15 seats to form next Melaka government, says EC
Article:
MELAKA: Barisan Nasional secured a simple majority after winning 15 of the 28 seats in the Melaka election as at 9.40pm.
Election Commission chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said the result enabled BN to form the state government with a simple majority.
He said that based on the results as at 9.40pm, BN had won 15 seats, while Pakatan Harapan secured two and Perikatan Nasional  one.
"BN has won 15 of the 28 seats contested, thereby securing more than 50 per cent of the total number of seats.
"As such, BN can form the state government with a simple majority," he said at an EC press conference.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Immigration arrest 205 foreigners in Senai raid
Article:
KULAI: Immigration authorities arrested 205 foreigners in an early-morning raid on several apartment blocks in Taman Desa Idaman, Senai, Johor.
The arrests were made during a joint operation by the Johor Immigration Department and the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency at 1.30am.
Immigration deputy director-general (Operations) Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli said those arrested were from Myanmar, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Nepal, Thailand, Pakistan and India.
Initial checks found that they had committed various offences under the Immigration Act 1959/63, including failing to produce identification documents and overstaying in Malaysia.
He said enforcement officers had checked 543 foreigners during the operation, including the 205 arrested, among them 57 women.
Drones were also used to monitor the foreigners' movements and identify the directions in which they might flee, he said.
During the operation, officers also raided a residential unit believed to have been converted into an entertainment venue for foreigners.
Lokman Effendi said the relevant authorities would take action over the matter.
Those arrested were taken to the Home Ministry Complex in Setia Tropika.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: BN-PN nominate Ab Rauf as CM
Article:
AYER KEROH: Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh has been nominated for a second term as Melaka Chief Minister following Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional's victory in 24 of the 28 state seats.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi announced the nomination tonight, saying Ab Rauf's letter of nomination would be submitted to Melaka Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
"Therefore, I hereby announce that Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional nominate Datuk Seri Dr Abdul Rauf Yusoh as the candidate for Melaka Chief Minister," he said.
Zahid was speaking after announcing BN-PN's unofficial victory at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here.
He said the 24-seat tally gave BN-PN a more than two-thirds majority, allowing the coalition to form the state government and continue the administration under Ab Rauf's leadership.
He said the result reflected voters' acceptance of the administrative track record, political stability and development direction offered by the two coalitions.
"This mandate of more than a two-thirds majority proves that the people of Melaka continue to choose the track record, stability and development direction offered by BN and PN over the political rhetoric played up throughout the campaign period," he said.
Zahid described the victory as a continuation of the "blue wave" momentum that began in Johor, spread to Negri Sembilan and had now gained further strength in Melaka.
He added that the strategic cooperation between BN and PN during the election would be further strengthened to ensure a stable, united and credible state government.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN-PN sweep 24 seats to secure Melaka victory
Article:
MELAKA: Continuing the momentum from the Johor and Negri Sembilan elections, Barisan Nasional, with the support of Perikatan Nasional, has returned to power in Melaka after securing a landslide victory in the state election, according to unofficial results.
The consolidation of Malay support following the electoral cooperation between BN and PN helped the two coalitions secure 24 of the 28 seats contested, giving them more than a two-thirds majority in the state assembly.
BN won 21 seats, while PN secured three through its component parties, Pas (two) and Parti Wawasan Negara (one). The latter also won its first seat in the state assembly.
The BN-PN alliance's first victory came when unofficial results showed that BN candidate Datuk Abdul Hakim Abdul Wahid had secured the Lendu seat with a majority of 5,752 votes.
Loud cheers and applause erupted at the Melaka International Trade Centre, which had been turned into BN's election results viewing centre, when unofficial results showed caretaker Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh had retained the Tanjung Bidara seat for a second term.
Rauf, who is also Melaka BN chairman, secured a majority of 9,114 votes, a significant increase from the 364-vote majority he obtained in the 2021 state election.
Unofficial results showed that Rauf polled 10,293 votes to defeat Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate Mohd Yunazri Mustamiri, who received 1,089 votes.
The jubilant atmosphere continued when unofficial results showed that Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh had retained the Merlimau seat, defeating PH candidate Rahayu Hamzah.
Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem, who has 1.5 million social media followers, also appeared to have translated his online popularity into electoral support by retaining the Duyong seat with a majority of 10,067 votes, according to unofficial results.
In the 2021 state election, Noor Helmy won the seat with a slim majority of 200 votes.
Another BN candidate, Datuk Khaidirah Abu Zahar, who was previously active in the entertainment industry, also retained the Rim seat in a straight fight against PH's Esma Eazreen Husin.
The sole MIC candidate, S. Nadarajah, one of eight new faces fielded by BN in the election, helped the coalition retain the Gadek seat. Unofficial results showed that the Melaka MIC deputy chairman won with a majority of 3,497 votes.
Unofficial results also showed that Melaka MCA chairman Datuk Lim Ban Hong and his deputy, Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem, had retained the Klebang and Machap Jaya seats respectively.
As of 9pm, unofficial results showed that BN had also secured Kuala Linggi, Ayer Limau, Lendu, Taboh Naning, Rembia, Durian Tunggal, Asahan, Sungai Udang, Pantai Kundor, Ayer Molek and Telok Mas, among other seats.
PN also contributed to the alliance's landslide victory when Pas candidate Muhammad Ridzuan Mohd Sarif pulled off a major upset by defeating PH's Amanah vice-president and former Melaka chief minister Adly Zahari in a four-cornered contest in Bukit Katil.
In the 2021 state election, Adly, who is now the deputy defence minister, won the seat with a majority of 1,057 votes.
Pas scored another upset in Paya Rumput when its candidate, Rafie Ahmad, defeated PH candidate Datuk Azman Abidin, who is also the prime minister's political secretary, in a three-cornered contest.
The seat was previously held by BN but was allocated to PN under the electoral cooperation agreement between the two coalitions for this election.
Parti Wawasan Negara won Bemban after its candidate, Dr Mohd Yadzil Yaakub, defeated three other challengers, including Dr Akmal's brother, Dr Muhammad Solehin Saleh, who contested as a Bersama candidate.
In the previous state election, Dr Yadzil won the seat as a Bersatu candidate.
Bersatu, meanwhile, lost all the seats it contested in the election.
DAP retained all four seats it contested, namely Kesidang, Ayer Keroh, Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir.
The BN-PN alliance's return to power in Melaka became increasingly clear when Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki announced at about 8pm that the two coalitions had unofficially surpassed the simple-majority threshold of 15 seats needed to form the next state government.
About 20 minutes later, Asyraf announced that BN-PN had unofficially secured a two-thirds majority after winning 19 seats.
The election also recorded a higher voter turnout than the 2021 state election, when turnout stood at 65.85 per cent.
According to the Election Commission's real-time Voter Turnout Monitoring dashboard, about 70 per cent of ordinary voters had cast their ballots by 6pm. Of the 28 state constituencies, Bandar Hilir recorded the lowest turnout at 57.7 per cent.
Political observers said the turnout reflected a strong mandate for the BN-PN alliance.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid: Melaka voters chose BN's track record and stability
Article:
AYER KEROH: Melaka voters had chosen a proven track record and stability over campaign rhetoric, Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman and Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said the incoming state administration would fulfil every manifesto promise.
After declaring an unofficial two-thirds majority win alongside Perikatan Nasional (PN), Zahid said the projected 24-seat mandate reflected public confidence in the coalition's development agenda.
"This mandate of more than a two-thirds majority proves that the people of Melaka continue to choose the track record, stability and development direction offered by BN and PN," he told supporters at the Melaka International Trade Centre.
Unofficial BN tallies showed BN winning 21 of the 28 state seats, while PN secured three and Pakatan Harapan (PH) four.
The Election Commission was expected to announce the official results by midnight.
Following BN's momentum in Johor and Negri Sembilan, Zahid said the projected victory was not a reason for arrogance, adding that the mandate carried a heavy responsibility to fulfil the manifesto for all Melakans, regardless of race, religion or background.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zahid says BN-PN hat-trick no reason for complacency
Article:
MELAKA: Barisan Nasional  will not allow its hat-trick of victories alongside Perikatan Nasional in Johor, Negri Sembilan and Melaka to become a reason for the coalitions to be complacent.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the latest victory in Melaka, where the two coalitions secured 24 of the 28 state seats according to unofficial results, reflected the growing momentum of the blue wave that began in Johor and continued in Negri Sembilan.
He said the coalition hoped the momentum would spread nationwide, allowing the people to choose a government capable of ensuring stability and delivering on their aspirations.
"This hat-trick of three consecutive victories is not a reason for us to boast. Instead, we receive it with gratitude, humility and a deep sense of responsibility.
"We are aware that the mandate entrusted to us carries a great responsibility to fulfil every manifesto pledge and provide the best possible service to all the people of Melaka, regardless of their religion, race or background," he said.
Zahid, who is also Umno president and deputy prime minister, said the 24-seat victory, which gave BN and PN more than a two-thirds majority in the state assembly, reflected the people's confidence in the coalitions' track record, stability and development plans.
"BN and PN have succeeded in forming the Melaka state government by winning 24 seats.
"The more than two-thirds majority shows that Melaka continues to choose the track record, stability and development direction offered by BN and PN," he said.
He said the election had also demonstrated that the political understanding between the two coalitions was growing stronger and gaining wider acceptance among the people.
Also present were Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UTS eyes integrative medical research using Sarawak's biodiversity, AI
Article:
SIBU: Universiti Teknologi Sarawak (UTS) could become a centre for integrative medical research, combining Eastern and Western medicine with Sarawak's biodiversity and artificial intelligence (AI) technology.
Its Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said the development of the university's medical faculty would create opportunities to explore new approaches to disease prevention and treatment, including cancer.
He said integrative medicine, which is gaining international attention, also emphasised salutogenesis, a concept that focuses on factors contributing to health and wellbeing.
"We have biodiversity that can serve as a foundation for research to find solutions to various diseases, including new ones.
"UTS can combine Eastern and Western medical expertise, in addition to using AI to analyse DNA and identify potential compounds for disease treatment," he said after the 11th UTS Convocation Ceremony.
Abang Johari said research into natural materials could also lead to the discovery of new treatment methods, particularly for cancer, but their effectiveness would need to be scientifically proven.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka polls: PH accepts voters' mandate, says Adly [WATCH]
Article:
MELAKA: Unofficial results put Pakatan Harapan winning only four of the 24 seats it contested in the 16th Melaka election, all through DAP.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the coalition it accepted the outcome with an open mind and respected the decision of the voters.
He said the four seats won by PH were Kota Laksamana, Kesidang, Ayer Keroh and Bandar Hilir.
"We accept this result as part of the democratic process and as an opportunity to strengthen our efforts moving forward.
"PH has always believed that election results are influenced by various dynamics, and there is always room for improvement in the future," he told reporters.
Adly said the coalition would conduct a comprehensive post-mortem to assess its performance, including its election manifesto, campaign strategies and voting patterns.
He said the findings would be brought before the PH Presidential Council for further deliberation.
According to unofficial results as of 9.04pm, PH's Allex Seah Shoo Chin secured the Kesidang seat with 19,781 votes, defeating Perikatan Nasional's Albert Kok, who received 10,672 votes, and Parti Bersama Malaysia's Dr Bryan Kek, who garnered 1,952 votes. Seah won with a majority of 9,109 votes.
In Kota Laksamana, PH's Low Chee Leong obtained 14,547 votes, defeating Bersama's Ethan Lim Zhi Hao, who received 5,097 votes, and Barisan Nasional's Melvin Chua, who secured 1,561 votes. Low won with a majority of 9,450 votes.
Meanwhile, PH's Leng Chau Yen secured Bandar Hilir with 9,804 votes, defeating BN's Jasmine Lok, who received 2,033 votes, and Bersama's Ir Dr Rashidi Jalil, who garnered 1,304 votes. Leng recorded a majority of 7,771 votes.
However, PH faced a much narrower contest in Ayer Keroh, where its candidate Kerk Chee Yee obtained 1,368 votes, defeating PN's Michael Gan, who secured 1,021 votes, by a majority of just 347 votes.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar arrives in Manila to lead Malaysia's mission at 49th Asean Summit
Article:
MANILA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has arrived in Manila, Philippines, to lead the Malaysian delegation at the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, which begin tomorrow and run until Nov 17.
The aircraft carrying Anwar and his delegation landed at Ninoy Aquino International Airport at 8pm.
Anwar was accompanied by his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, and was welcomed by Philippine Interior and Local Government Secretary Juanito Victor "Jonvic" C. Remulla Jr.
Also present were Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, Foreign Ministry secretary-general Tan Sri Amran Mohamed Zin and Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Datuk Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino Anthony.
The Malaysian delegation also includes Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani.
"Malaysia will continue to play an active role in strengthening regional ties, fostering mutual understanding and expanding cooperation for the sake of peace, stability and shared prosperity.
I seek everyone's prayers that the journey and all engagements will go smoothly, and that this mission will yield meaningful outcomes for Malaysia and the entire Asean region," Anwar wrote in a Facebook post.
Tomorrow, Anwar is scheduled to attend the 49th Asean Summit, comprising the Plenary and Retreat Sessions, as well as three engagement sessions with the Asean Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA), Asean Business Advisory Council (Asean-BAC) and Asean youth representatives.
He is also scheduled to attend four summits with dialogue partners: the 29th Asean-China Summit, 16th Asean-United Nations Summit, sixth Asean-Australia Summit and 27th Asean-Republic of Korea Summit.
Besides bilateral meetings with several counterparts from Asean member states, the 12th Asean-United States Special Summit will also be among the key events.
Malaysia's participation in this summit is important in safeguarding the country's interests while reinforcing its active role in shaping Asean's future direction.
The high-level engagement will also allow Malaysia to contribute to regional discussions and policymaking across political and security, economic, and socio-cultural areas.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Italy fines Meta US$887 million over Android users' data access
Article:
MILAN: Italy's data protection agency said on Saturday it had fined Meta Platforms €805 million (US$887 million) after finding that the company had accessed Android users' photographs and videos without obtaining their consent or informing them.
Meta had access to Android users' photos and videos through a Facebook app feature that suggested content from users' personal galleries that they could post, the authority said in a statement.
Meta has 60 days to disable the feature by default and seek users' consent separately, it added.
Meta was not immediately available for comment.
The investigation, which began in 2025, did not cover the possible use of the content to train artificial intelligence models, a practice Meta denied, the authority said.
It added that it reserved the right to assess separately a new feature, launched in 2026, that allows content from users' galleries to be processed in the cloud.
The fine is equivalent to about 0.47 per cent of the group's global revenue, the authority said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Health Ministry reports cyber breach at facility, services unaffected
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A cyber incident at a Health Ministry facility involved unauthorised access to a file storage and sharing platform but did not disrupt healthcare services, the ministry said.
A preliminary investigation by the ministry's Computer Security Incident Response Team found that the incident did not involve encryption of its main databases.
The incident occurred on Nov 12 and was limited to a supporting file storage and sharing platform at one of its facilities.
"The incident was limited to unauthorised access to a supporting file storage and sharing platform at a ministry facility," it said in a statement.
As an immediate containment measure, public access to the platform has been blocked.
The ministry said it had also put additional security controls in place at the facility, including resetting user passwords, auditing servers and enforcing multi-factor authentication.
"The ministry confirms that all main operating systems as well as health services and patient treatment are not affected and are operating as usual.
"The public may continue with health appointments and treatment at ministry facilities without any worry," it said.
The ministry said it would continue working closely with the National Cyber Security Agency, in line with the Cyber Security Act 2024, and carry out continuous monitoring.
"The ministry issues a stern warning that downloading, possessing or spreading official government documents obtained illegally is a serious offence subject to legal action," it added.
It said it remained committed to keeping its information technology infrastructure secure and the public's health data confidential.
The statement comes after the government
raised the National Cyber Threat Level
from low to moderate on Nov 4.
On Nov 3, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told the Dewan Rakyat that Malaysia was among countries considered
potential targets of cyberattacks.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UNOFFICIAL] BN-PN secure 24 seats in Melaka election, says Zahid
Article:
MELAKA: Barisan Nasional, together with its electoral partner Perikatan Nasional, has won 24 of the 28 seats contested, according to unofficial results.
The announcement was made by BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi during a press conference at the Melaka International Trade Centre, which had been turned into BN's election results viewing centre.
Also present were several top BN leaders and PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MBPP shuts 10 unlicensed premises run by foreigners
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Ten unlicensed business premises, believed to be operated by foreigners, have been ordered to close in two enforcement operations by the Penang Island City Council (MBPP).
Their equipment was also seized during the operations.
In separate posts on its Facebook page, MBPP said the operations, conducted under Ops Tegas, targeted seven premises around Komtar, Air Itam and Gelugor on Thursday, followed by three more in Batu Ferringhi and Seri Tanjung Pinang yesterday.
"The operation focused on unlicensed business activities, premises managed or operated by foreigners, and breaches of local authority licensing conditions.
"Inspections also uncovered the involvement of foreigners at these premises, including people who failed to produce valid identification documents," the city council said.
MBPP said enforcement action against the 10 premises included closure orders, equipment seizures, confiscation of goods and the removal of signboards, depending on the offences committed.
Among the items seized were stoves, sinks, food racks, cutting tools and other business equipment, while horizontal signboards and banners were also removed.
The premises were sealed with safety tape to ensure business activities ceased immediately until all licensing breaches and public nuisance issues were resolved.
"Written notices were also issued to the relevant parties, instructing them not to remove or damage the sealing tape, trespass on the premises, or continue operating inside or outside the buildings," it added.
The enforcement action was carried out under the Local Government Act 1976, which empowers local authorities to safeguard public safety, health and comfort.
MBPP said that Ops Tegas would continue without compromise against those operating unlicensed businesses, involving foreigners who flout regulations, breaching licence conditions or causing public nuisance.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UNOFFICIAL] Melaka polls: PN wrests Bukit Katil from Adly Zahari
Article:
AYER KEROH: Perikatan Nasional (PN) has unofficially captured the Bukit Katil state seat from two-term Pakatan Harapan (PH) Adly Zahari in the 16th Melaka state election, according to Barisan Nasional's (BN) election tally.
Based on BN's unofficial count as of 8.40pm, PN candidate Muhammad Ridzuan Mohd Sarif (PAS) garnered 12,271 votes to take the constituency with a commanding majority of 5,584 votes.
The four-cornered contest also featured Bersama's candidate Dr Aliza Che Amran and independent candidate Abu Bakar Sabudin.
Bukit Katil is one of the constituencies allocated to PN under the Muafakat Melaka electoral pact—a political cooperation agreement signed between BN and PN on Oct 29 ahead of the state polls.
Under the pact, which also brings together supporting non-governmental organisations including Muafakat Nasional, BN contested 22 of the 28 state seats while PN fielded candidates in the remaining six constituencies without three-cornered clashes between the two coalitions.
The upset ends a two-term hold on Bukit Katil by Adly, who is also Amanah vice-president and Alor Gajah MP.
Adly first won the seat in the 2018 general election with a 3,159-vote majority before defending it in the 2021 state polls with a narrower 1,057-vote margin.
Located under the Hang Tuah Jaya parliamentary constituency, Bukit Katil has 35,359 registered voters, comprising roughly 64.8 per cent Malay, 28.7 per cent Chinese, 4.7 per cent Indian, and 1.8 per cent other voters.
Official results are expected to be delivered by the Election Commission (EC) at midnight.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UNOFFICIAL] Akmal Saleh retains Merlimau
Article:
MELAKA: Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh has retained the Merlimau seat for a second term, according to unofficial results.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki claimed Dr Akmal won the seat with a majority of 8,726 votes.
He said Dr Akmal polled 11,705 votes against Pakatan Harapan candidate Rahayu Hamzah, who received 2,979 votes.

Title: [UNOFFICIAL] Melaka polls: Noor Helmy retains Duyong with massive 10,067-vote majority
Article:
AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional (BN) incumbent Datuk Mohd Noor Helmy Abdul Halem has unofficially retained the Duyong state seat with a commanding 10,067-vote majority in the 16th Melaka state election.
According to unofficial party tallies, Noor Helmy garnered 15,064 votes to decisively defeat Pakatan Harapan (PH) challenger Poo Long Suan, who polled 4,997 votes.
The result marks a dramatic turnaround from the 2021 state election, when Noor Helmy won the seat by a razor-thin 200-vote majority.
Duyong, an urban-suburban mixed constituency under the Kota Melaka parliamentary seat, comprises roughly 63.8 per cent Malay, 29.9 per cent Chinese, and 4.8 per cent Indian voters.
The seat had been held by DAP for two consecutive terms. It was previously won by Goh Leong San in 2013 and Damian Yeo Shen Li in 2018 before Noor Helmy wrested it back for BN in a six-cornered contest in 2021 with 4,684 votes against Yeo's 4,484.
Following the 2021 polls, Noor Helmy was appointed Melaka Deputy Exco for Science, Technology, Innovation, and Digital Communication.
Official results is expected to be announced by the Election Commission (EC) at midnight.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UNOFFICIAL] BN-PN claim two-thirds majority in Melaka election [WATCH]
Article:
MELAKA: Barisan Nasional claimed it has secured two-thirds majority in the Melaka election.
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said this after BN together with its electoral partner Perikatan Nasional had secured a first-past-the-post (FPTP) victory in 21 constituencies.

Title: [UNOFFICIAL] Anwar's political secretary loses Paya Rumput contest
Article:
MELAKA: Political secretary to the Prime Minister Datuk Azman Abidin has lost the contest for the Paya Rumput seat in the Melaka election, according to unofficial results.
This follows Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki's announcement that Perikatan Nasional (PN) had secured a first-past-the-post (FPTP) victory in the constituency.
Unofficial results showed PN candidate Rafie Ahmad winning with a majority of 6,008 votes after polling 15,577 votes.
Azman garnered 9,569 votes, while Bersama candidate Abdul Rashid Abu Bakar received 1,011 votes.

Title: 29 Penang schools receive upgrades ahead of 2027 intake
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Twenty-nine schools in Penang have received infrastructure improvements ahead of the 2027 Year One intake.
The Penang Education Department said the work across five districts involved constructing additional buildings using the Industrialised Building System (IBS), as well as maintenance, renovation and classroom upgrades.
The upgrades were aimed at increasing school capacity and providing pupils with a more conducive, comfortable and safe learning environment, the department said in several Facebook posts.
In Seberang Prai Utara, 13 schools involving 1,336 pupils benefited from the initiative. Six underwent classroom maintenance and upgrades, while seven received additional IBS buildings.
Classroom upgrades were carried out at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Bertam Putra, SK Tasek Gelugor, SK Padang Menora, SK Pasir Gebu, SK Mak Mandin and SK Pinang Tunggal.
Additional IBS buildings were constructed at SK Paya Keladi, SK Bertam Indah, SK Pokok Sena, SK Sungai Dua, SK Taman Senangan, SK Lahar Yooi and SK Desa Murni.
In the Southwest district, five schools received infrastructure improvements. Additional IBS buildings were constructed at SK Sungai Pinang, SK Telok Bahang and SK Mutiara Perdana, while classroom renovations and upgrades were carried out at SK Sungai Rusa and SK Mutiara Perdana.
In the Northeast district, four schools were involved. SK Tanjong Tokong and SK Sungai Gelugor underwent classroom maintenance and upgrades, while additional IBS buildings were constructed at SK Tanjung Bunga and SK Jelutong Barat.
In Seberang Prai Tengah, three schools — SK Bukit Teh, SK Macang Bubok and SK Alma Jaya — received additional IBS buildings, benefiting 175 pupils.
In Seberang Prai Selatan, four schools benefited from both initiatives. Additional IBS buildings were constructed at SK Sungai Kechil and SK Bandar Tasek Mutiara, while classroom renovations and upgrades were carried out at SK Saujana Indah and SK Batu Kawan.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UNOFFICIAL] PM's political secretary trails in Paya Rumput race
Article:
MELAKA: Political secretary to the Prime Minister, Datuk Azman Abidin, is trailing in the contest for the Paya Rumput seat, according to unofficial results.
As of 7.58pm, Azman, the Pakatan Harapan candidate, had garnered 7,867 votes. Perikatan Nasional candidate Rafie Ahmad was leading the three-cornered contest with 12,327 votes.
