Title: [UNOFFICIAL] Melaka polls: BN bags 15 seats, enough to form state government
Article:
AYER KEROH: Barisan Nasional (BN) has unofficially secured 15 seats in the 16th Melaka state election, crossing the simple majority threshold required to form the next state government alongside its Muafakat Melaka partner, Perikatan Nasional (PN).
Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said Kuala Linggi, Serkam, Rembia, and Gadek were the latest constituencies to join BN's winning tally.
"Unofficially, this completes our numbers — together with our PN partner under Muafakat Melaka, we have succeeded in forming the Melaka state government," he said at the BN election watch party at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC).
The four constituencies join BN's earlier unofficial wins in Sungai Udang (14,152 votes), Duyong (13,004), Asahan (9,830), Merlimau (9,640), Rim (8,685), Tanjung Bidara (8,210), Sungai Rambai (7,838), Ayer Limau (7,619), Lendu (7,311), Taboh Naning (5,795), and Machap Jaya (5,311).
A simple majority of 15 seats in the 28-member Melaka State Legislative Assembly is required to form the state administration, while 19 seats secure a two-thirds supermajority.
In this election, BN contested 23 seats under its Muafakat Melaka pact with PN, which fielded candidates in the remaining five constituencies.
Official results is expected to be announced by the Election Commission (EC) at midnight.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man fatally stabbed while trying to stop suspect chasing food vendor
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A man was fatally stabbed at a staircase beside a business premises in Sulaman Sentral, Kuala Manggatal, early today.
The 31-year-old victim is believed to have been trying to stop a suspect from chasing a food vendor following an argument between the two over a business-related disagreement.
Kota Kinabalu deputy district police chief, Superintendent Syed Lot, Syed Abdul Rahman said preliminary investigations found that the suspect had initially argued with the food vendor before attempting to stab him with a folding knife.
However, the vendor managed to evade the attack and flee, prompting the suspect to chase him.
"The victim, a local man who was at a snooker centre with his friend at the time, is believed to have tried to stop the suspect from continuing to chase the vendor.
"The suspect is then believed to have taken a meat cleaver before encountering the victim on a staircase on the first floor, near a business premises.
"The suspect allegedly stabbed the victim in the right side of his chest. The victim tried to flee but collapsed in a nearby parking area," he said in a statement today.
Lot said the victim's family rushed to the scene after receiving a call and took him to Sabah Women and Children's Hospital in Likas for emergency treatment.
However, the victim was pronounced dead at 6.44am.
The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
Members of the public with information about the incident are urged to assist investigations by contacting the Kota Kinabalu district police headquarters hotline at 088-529222 or any nearby police station.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN-PN sweep Melaka in 24-seat landslide, Pakatan reduced to just four urban seats
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 14 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) have stormed to an emphatic two-thirds supermajority in the Melaka state election, capturing a combined 24 of the 28 state assembly seats, according to unofficial results tonight.
In a sweeping victory that consolidated the ruling coalition's regional dominance, BN triumphed in 21 constituencies on its own, matching its 2021 seat benchmark, while PN captured three seats.
The joint tally of 24 seats represents one more than the two coalitions achieved when contesting separately five years ago, decimating Pakatan Harapan (PH) to just four urban enclaves.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi thanked voters across the state for delivering a resounding mandate, while Amanah leader Adly Zahari conceded defeat on behalf of PH, stating that the coalition would focus on rebuilding its grassroots strength.
Incumbent Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh secured an unassailable mandate to remain at the helm of the state administration, retaining his Tanjung Bidara seat with an unofficial majority of 8,650 votes, an exponential increase from the razor-thin 364-vote margin he secured in 2021.
BN also registered runaway majorities across rural and semi-urban bastions, led by a 12,036-vote cushion in Sungai Udang, which it successfully wrested back from PN, and 11,742 votes in Serkam.
BN's closest battle unfolded in Machap Jaya, where it held off a determined charge from PH's Ginie Lim by 1,925 votes after trailing in early ballot boxes.
PH suffered major political casualties across the state, losing former chief minister Adly in his Bukit Katil backyard to PN's Ridzuan Sarif.
The federal ruling pact took another severe hit in Paya Rumput, where Azman Abidin, political secretary to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, was ousted by PN.
PH was ultimately reduced to its four traditional urban Chinese-majority strongholds of Kesidang, Ayer Keroh, Kota Laksamana, and Bandar Hilir, each retained by DAP with comfortable margins surpassing 5,000 votes as MCA failed to reclaim lost ground.
PN's three victories were swept entirely by PAS-affiliated candidates, who retained Bemban while capturing Bukit Katil and Paya Rumput out of the five seats allocated to the coalition.
Conversely, Bersatu suffered a humiliating statewide wipeout after fielding candidates in seven seats under its own logo following an acrimonious split with PAS. The party was dismantled in Sungai Udang, where its candidate polled just 1,522 votes against the winner's 13,558, with its best showing in Pantai Kundor still leaving Dr Asmah Samat trailing BN's Tuminah Kadi by 2,177 votes.
Newcomer Parti Bersama Malaysia again failed to win any of the seats it contested, while independent contenders were similarly shut out.

Title: Zahid confirms Ab Rauf as Melaka CM after BN-PN supermajority win
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 14 — Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) will nominate incumbent Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh to continue leading the Melaka government following their two-thirds majority in the 16th state election tonight.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the letter of appointment for Ab Rauf would be submitted to Melaka Yang Dipertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam tonight.
He announced this after declaring the pact’s two-thirds majority win at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh here.
Unofficial results as of 9.20 pm showed BN and PN winning 24 of the 28 seats in the Melaka State Legislative Assembly.
Pakatan Harapan (PH) won the remaining four. — Bernama

Title: ‘Much to explain and reflect upon’: Pakatan accepts Melaka election setback, says state chief
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 14 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) has accepted the outcome of the Melaka state election and respects the people’s mandate despite winning only four of the 24 state assembly seats it contested, according to unofficial results.
Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said the coalition would use the results to assess its performance and strengthen efforts to regain public confidence.
“PH has always believed that election outcomes are shaped by various dynamics and that there is room for improvement in the future,” he told a press conference at the coalition’s main operations centre here tonight.
Adly said the results would also be brought before the PH Presidential Council for a comprehensive review, taking into account previous state election outcomes, including those in Johor and Negeri Sembilan.
“I believe PH will have much to explain and reflect upon following today’s results in Melaka,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Tok Mat says South China Sea code talks nearly 90pc complete, Malaysia pushing for deal by this year
Article:
MANILA, Nov 14 — Nearly 90 per cent of the proposed Code of Conduct (COC) in the South China Sea has been agreed upon by Asean and China, with Malaysia optimistic that negotiations can be concluded soon.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said negotiations were in their final stage, although several outstanding issues still required political decisions.
He said certain sensitive terms and provisions also needed mutual agreement among the countries involved.
“Malaysia, as the country coordinator for Asean-China relations, is committed to ensuring that the negotiations are concluded as soon as possible.
“Nearly 90 per cent of the terms, paragraphs and wording in the document have been agreed upon. However, some words may be sensitive to certain countries but not to others,” he told Malaysian journalists after attending Asean foreign ministers’ meetings here today.
Mohamad said the three-year target previously set to conclude the COC negotiations would expire this year, with efforts now focused on aligning the positions of the littoral states involved.
Asean and China have intensified negotiations this year, holding monthly meetings to resolve outstanding issues, including the COC’s legal status, geographical scope, and relationship with the 2002 Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea (DOC).
Both sides are aiming to conclude negotiations on the COC by the end of this year. — Bernama

Title: George Town slashing video circulating online is week-old, man has been jailed, say police
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 14 — The suspect involved in the incident where a man was slashed with a knife in front of Sekolah Kebangsaan Batu Lancang here, as seen in the viral video of the incident on social media today, had already been arrested by the police the day after the incident.
Timur Laut district police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said that based on the investigation, the incident occurred at 2.07pm on November 4 and is believed to have stemmed from the suspect’s dissatisfaction with the victim’s driving.
The police detected a video of the incident that went viral on social media today. The incident occurred on November 4 and a 30-year-old man had been arrested.
“The 54-year-old victim suffered lacerations to the right arm and abdomen due to a knife used by the suspect in the incident,” he said in a statement today.
It is said that the case was investigated under Section 324 of the Penal Code and the suspect was charged in court on November 11 and pleaded guilty before being sentenced to eight months in prison.
According to him, in this regard, the police advise the public not to spread the video or make any speculation that could cause concern among the community. — Bernama

Title: Anwar lands in Manila for Asean summit before brief dash back to meet Macron
Article:
MANILA, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived here tonight for the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, with a packed diplomatic schedule that will see him return briefly to Malaysia to receive French President Emmanuel Macron before flying back to Manila.
The special aircraft carrying Anwar and his wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, landed at Terminal 2 of Ninoy Aquino International Airport at 8pm.
He was received by Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, Foreign Ministry Secretary-General Tan Sri Amran Mohamed Zin, and Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Datuk Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino Anthony.
Also present was the Secretary of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) of the Philippines, Sec. Juanito Victor “Jonvic” C. Remulla Jr.
Tomorrow, Anwar is scheduled to attend the 49th Asean Summit Plenary and Retreat sessions, followed by engagements with the Asean Inter-Parliamentary Assembly (AIPA), Asean Business Advisory Council (Asean-BAC) and Asean youth representatives.
On Monday (November 16), he will attend Asean summits with key dialogue partners, including China, the United Nations, Australia and South Korea.
Anwar is scheduled to return to Malaysia later that day to receive French President Emmanuel Macron, who will make an official visit on the morning of November 17, before flying back to Manila that afternoon.
Upon his return, he will attend the Asean-United States Special Summit and an official dinner hosted by Philippine President Ferdinand Romualdez Marcos Jr.
Mohamad will lead Malaysia’s delegation to the 29th Asean Plus Three Summit, the fourth Asia Zero Emission Community (AZEC) Leaders’ Meeting, Asean summits with Japan and India, and the 21st East Asia Summit (EAS) during Anwar’s absence.
Anwar is also expected to hold several bilateral meetings with his Asean counterparts on the sidelines of the summits.
Malaysia’s delegation includes Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and senior officials from relevant ministries and agencies.
The annual summit meetings were preceded by four ministerial-level meetings today, including an Extended Informal Consultation on the Implementation of the Five-Point Consensus (5PC) on Myanmar.
At an earlier media briefing for Malaysian journalists, Abdul Malik said Anwar’s participation would enable Malaysia to help shape regional policies on political and security matters, economic cooperation and sociocultural issues.
“This summit provides a strategic platform to engage directly with leaders of Asean member states and dialogue partners, fostering dialogue on pressing shared challenges while strengthening key bilateral ties,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Police yet to receive further instructions on Shuhaily’s return from border control agency, says IGP
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 14 — Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) Director-General Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain continues to perform his duties as usual as no further instructions have been issued regarding his position.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the police had yet to receive any further instructions on whether Mohd Shuhaily would be returned to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
“As I have explained before, Datuk Seri Shuhaily is a police officer who is serving a two-year contract as AKPS Director-General.
“His appointment was made by the King. Therefore, I am awaiting further instructions should he be returned to PDRM for further action. So far, no such instructions have been received,” he said at a press conference after visiting the polling centre at Sekolah Kebangsaan Tun Syed Ahmad Shahabudin in Ayer Keroh here today.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail was reported to have said earlier today that the ministry had yet to decide on the appointment of a new AKPS Director-General to replace Mohd Shuhaily.
He was reported as saying that the ministry had given its assurance that AKPS operations would continue as usual and would not be affected by the decision to return Mohd Shuhaily to his parent organisation, PDRM. — Bernama

Title: Learn from Indonesia, tighten export monitoring to stop under-invoicing, say industry players
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Stricter monitoring of commodity exports is needed to curb under-invoicing, a practice in which exporters declare lower cargo values or quantities than what they actually ship, potentially causing losses in government revenue, maritime industry players said.
Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said Indonesia’s move to set up a centralised agency to monitor major commodity exports should remind Malaysia to review how effective its own export monitoring systems are.
It was reported that Indonesia’s Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia (DSI), operated by sovereign wealth fund Danantara, will initially oversee exports worth about US$60 billion involving coal, palm oil and ferroalloys.
The agency plans to introduce a service fee in the single-digit US dollar range per tonne, with the final rate expected to be announced in December. It is scheduled to begin full operations in January 2027.
The initiative aims to improve monitoring of commodity exports and tackle practices such as under-invoicing, which can allow exporters to avoid paying the full taxes or duties due on their shipments.
Jeyenderan said Malaysia already had various electronic systems and government agencies responsible for monitoring export declarations, permits and supporting documents.
However, he said the bigger challenge was ensuring that information held by different agencies could be properly shared and cross-checked against actual cargo shipments.
“Having digital systems is important, but what matters is whether the information can be cross-checked to ensure that the quantity and value declared in the documents match the actual goods being exported,” he said in a statement.
He said discrepancies between declared values or quantities and actual cargo shipments could affect government revenue, create unfair competition among businesses and undermine confidence in Malaysia’s commodity trade.
Maritime Network managing director Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said Malaysia already had various electronic systems and government agencies responsible for monitoring export declarations, permits and supporting documents.— Bernama pic
Jeyenderan said Malaysia should consider whether its existing systems could be better integrated so authorities can track export information from the time goods are declared and loaded onto vessels until the shipments reach their destinations.
He said this was particularly important for commodities such as palm oil and petroleum, where large volumes of cargo pass through ports and may involve several parties, including exporters, shipping companies, storage operators and buyers.
“Authorities should be able to establish whether the goods declared by an exporter are consistent with the actual cargo loaded onto the vessel and the documents accompanying the shipment,” he said.
He said better coordination between the Royal Malaysian Customs Department, port authorities, commodity regulators and shipping operators could help identify discrepancies earlier and reduce the risk of revenue leakage.
Meanwhile, maritime analyst and scholar Nazery Khalid said that while it was understandable for multiple agencies to be involved in the process, they should break down institutional silos and work more closely together.
He said this was important to ensure documentation, monitoring, inspections, testing and enforcement were carried out effectively and transparently.
Nazery said digital technology should also be used to help the agencies coordinate, so they can share data and improve visibility across supply chains.
“This would allow the agencies to make more informed, data-driven decisions and strengthen oversight of commodity exports.
“This would also strengthen confidence in Malaysia’s export and trading systems, prevent revenue leakages such as unpaid taxes and unaccounted foreign exchange outflows, and mitigate public health risks arising from the misdeclaration of commingled cargo, such as blended palm oil,” Nazery said.

Title: Police refer 32 Melaka election cases to AGC, including alleged seditious speeches
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 14 — Police have submitted 32 investigation papers related to the 16th Melaka State Election to the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) and are now awaiting further instructions.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said 42 police reports were received during the 14-day campaign period, on issues including the tearing down and burning of flags, as well as speeches by several individuals alleged to have contained seditious elements.
“We have opened 32 investigation papers. I believe and am confident that the police will conduct the best possible investigation professionally, without bias towards any side or party,” he said at a press conference at Sekolah Kebangsaan Tun Syed Ahmad Shahabudin in Ayer Keroh here today.
Asked about a campaign speech by an influential individual from a political party, Mohd Khalid said police had completed the investigation paper on the matter and submitted it to the AGC.
“We investigated under Sections 505 and 298 of the Penal Code. The individual concerned will also be called to have his statement recorded,” he said.
Regarding security on polling day, Mohd Khalid said the situation in the state remained under control as of this afternoon, with no incidents of concern throughout the process.
He said about 3,300 police officers and personnel have been deployed to maintain security and public order during the state election, comprising about 1,500 personnel from Melaka and another 1,800 from other states.
He said the deployment covered security control at polling centres and channels as well as public places, along with traffic management in cooperation with various agencies and ministries.
Mohd Khalid said that once polling closes at 6pm, police will secure vote-tallying centres, which are expected to draw crowds of supporters.
“I hope there will be no processions to celebrate victories and so on. Everyone must observe proper conduct and uphold the law to ensure everything runs well and smoothly,” he said.
The 16th Melaka State Election involves 28 state assembly seats.
For the latest news on the 16th Melaka State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: No disruption to border control agency after director-general’s transfer, says Saifuddin Nasution
Article:
LUMUT, Nov 14 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) continues to operate as usual nationwide, unaffected by the decision to return its director-general to his parent organisation, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said as the officer was on secondment from the police force, further administrative matters would be handled by the relevant agency, pending the appointment of a successor.
“We have not reached that stage (of appointing an AKPS director-general) yet. Let’s settle things one at a time. However, I can assure you that AKPS operations will not be affected because the agency plays an important role, as its name suggests — the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency.
“We cannot allow the entire organisation to come to a standstill just because its director-general is involved in a transfer. That is not how it should be,” he told reporters after officiating the Madani Kita Programme (PMK) and the 2026 handover ceremony for the People’s Volunteer Corps’ (Rela) Kampung Angkat Madani (Madani Adopted Village) and Sekolah Angkat Madani (Madani Adopted School) initiatives at Kampung Sungai Tiram here today.
He was responding to a question on the current status of the AKPS director-general’s position and when it was expected to be filled.
He said Home Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman had been directed to give special attention to the agency’s management, while any court proceedings would be allowed to take their course in accordance with the law.
Saifuddin Nasution added that field reports showed that AKPS personnel remained effective in carrying out their duties, having foiled several smuggling attempts, including the recent arrest of two individuals who attempted to bring a large sum of cash through a route to Singapore.
On October 29, the Home Ministry decided that AKPS director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain would return to duty with the PDRM.
Mohd Shuhaily was appointed AKPS director-general for a two-year term from July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2027.
On October 21, Mohd Shuhaily pleaded not guilty at the Sepang Magistrate’s Court to two charges of causing injuries to two police personnel at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) on September 28.
Meanwhile, on today’s programme, Saifuddin Nasution said the government had allocated RM500,000 for improvement works at four locations under the Madani Adopted Village initiative, and RM100,000 for a school under the Madani Adopted School initiative, bringing the total allocation to RM600,000.
The four Madani Adopted Village locations comprise Masjid Al-Ismailiah, where a cooking hall, storage room and covered walkway will be built; Sekolah Rendah Agama Rakyat (SRAR) Al-Hidayah, where the building will be repaired and the fence replaced; Surau Haji Lot, where the open-sided hall, cooking hall and women’s prayer area will be upgraded; and Surau Parit Haji Dollah, where handrails, a PA system, new carpets and solar lights will be installed.
Meanwhile, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Sungai Tiram received an allocation under Madani Adopted School for painting works, replacement of gutters and maintenance of its four-storey building, as well as the conservation of its heritage wooden school building, including termite treatment, to improve the comfort of the school community.
“We have 11 agencies, each implementing one programme, and this is now the third year of the initiative. This means we have reached at least 33 villages, with allocations ranging from RM500,000 to RM1 million. The good thing is that none of the projects we have undertaken has been abandoned,” he said.
The PMK, which brought together about 2,000 participants, also featured various community and spiritual activities, including congregational Subuh prayers, religious talks, Rela’s Ziarah Kasih visits to the homes of two underprivileged residents, as well as free services such as haircuts and motorcycle engine oil changes, alongside Rahmah and Agro Madani Sales. — Bernama

Title: 2026 Melaka State Election: Zahid thanks voters for BN-PN’s decisive 24-seat win
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 14 —
[9.25pm]
Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has thanked Melaka voters for the mandate given to his coalition and Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the state election, in a statement issued on behalf of both parties.
The thanks follow an unofficial claim of a sweeping win by the BN-PN side, with BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki saying the two have won 24 of the 28 state seats, a clear supermajority in the state assembly.
If the claim holds, BN and PN together have taken all but four seats, which would leave Pakatan Harapan (PH) with just four, consistent with the seat-by-seat figures reported earlier, which showed PH holding only its urban seats of Kesidang, Ayer Keroh, Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir.
PH has conceded the results. Amanah’s Adly Zahari, a former Melaka CM, who lost his Bukit Katil seat to PN, said the coalition accepts the results and will focus on strengthening its efforts going forward.
The result will be read as a setback for PH, after DAP left the state government in July and the coalition went into the election as a rival to BN.
BN and PN are expected to work together in Melaka, but how formal that cooperation will be has not yet been spelled out. The figures remain unofficial until the Election Commission confirms the final results.
[8.45pm]
Barisan Nasional (BN) has won the Melaka state election, with unofficial results as of about 8.35pm showing it past the 15 seats needed to form the government on its own.
Of the 24 seats declared so far, BN has taken 19, Pakatan Harapan (PH) four and Perikatan Nasional (PN) one. Four seats were still outstanding at that point: Bukit Katil, Paya Rumput, Kelebang and Ayer Molek.
BN’s results are decisive. Its biggest majorities came in Serkam (11,742 votes), Sungai Udang (12,036) and Telok Mas (10,903). It also captured Sungai Udang from PN, which held the seat in 2021, and kept Machap Jaya by 1,925 votes against PH’s Ginie Lim, after PH had led there at 7.19pm. Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh retained Tanjung Bidara with an unofficial majority of 8,650 votes, compared with just 364 in 2021.
PH’s results were concentrated in urban seats. It held Kesidang, Ayer Keroh, Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir, all by margins of over 5,000 votes, so MCA did not take the DAP seats it had said it was targeting.
PH’s worst result so far is in Bukit Katil, where PN’s Ridzuan Sarif leads Amanah’s Adly Zahari, who won the seat in 2021, by 3,224 votes. PN has also held Bemban and is claiming Paya Rumput, where BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki’s has announced a PN win over PH’s Azman Abidin, the pime minister’s political secretary.
The new party Parti Bersama Malaysia, which contested 16 seats, has not won any of the 24 declared so far, and neither has Bersatu. Bersama’s candidates have been well behind in each seat where they stood, which suggests the new party has not yet become a major factor in the vote.
If Asyraf’s declarations for Ayer Molek, Kelebang and Paya Rumput hold, BN would finish on 21 seats, matching its 2021 result, with PH on four and PN on three.
[8.30pm]
The Election Commission has announced unofficial BN wins in Serkam, Ayer Limau, Merlimau, Tanjung Bidara, Rim and Ayer Molek, and a PH win in Bandar Hilir.
BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki has also declared BN wins in Ayer Molek and Kelebang, and a PN win in Paya Rumput. Those are party announcements, not yet confirmed by the EC.
Major develoments include caretaker Chief Minister Ab Rauf Yusoh retaining Tanjung Bidara with an unofficial majority of 8,650 votes, up from just 364 in 2021.
BN has so far claimed 17 seats: the 12 in the earlier list plus Rembia, Kuala Linggi, Gadek, Ayer Molek and Kelebang. PN has Paya Rumput, and PH has Bandar Hilir.
BN’s seats already allow it to form the state government by simple majority.
[8.05pm]
Barisan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said BN-PN has won 15 seats, the simple majority needed to form the Melaka government.
BN itself has declared unofficial wins in 14 seats. The two coalitions are also on track for a supermajority.
[7.50pm]
Barisan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi has announced unofficial BN wins in Taboh Naning, Sungai Udang, Lendu and Tanjung Bidara, which is Chief Minister Ab Rauf’s seat.
These are BN’s own claims and have not been confirmed by the Election Commission.
[7.30pm]
With all 28 seats having partial counts, BN leads in 17, PH in 7, PN in 3 and Bersatu in 1. A minimum of 15 is needed for a majority. Bersama is not leading anywhere, putting it on track for another duck.
Close contests are forming in Machap Jaya, where PH has overtaken BN by 419 votes and Kuala Linggi (by 257), both seats where BN led in the earlier counts. PN leads PH in Paya Rumput by 172, and Bersatu’s Dr Asmah Samat leads BN’s Tuminah Kadi in Pantai Kundor by only 27.
Caretaker Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusof leads comfortably in Tanjung Bidara (2,510 votes to PH’s 335 from 2,845 counted). DAP-held Kota Laksamana and Bandar Hilir have PH well ahead of MCA, by 5,002 and 2,666 votes respectively.
[7.15pm]
BN is ahead in 13 of the 20 seats reporting so far, PH leads in five and PN in two, and Bersama is not leading in any of them.
PH leads in DAP’s strongholds of Kota Laksamana (1,459 votes to BN’s 356) and Bandar Hilir (849 to 154), with no sign of the MCA gains it was aiming for. Both are early counts, so margins could change.
[6.00pm]
Melaka voters cast their ballots today to elect a new state legislative assembly, in a high-stakes election that serves as a critical test of Barisan Nasional's (BN) traditional fortress and the increasingly strained federal partnership between it and Pakatan Harapan (PH).
A total of 675,166 eligible ordinary electors were registered to vote across 240 polling stations statewide, which operated from 8.00am to 6.00pm.
Turnout at 5pm had reached the 70 per cent target set by the Election Commission, which indicated that it expects initial ballot returns to arrive by around 9.30pm, with a comprehensive final tally anticipated before midnight.
The battle for the 28-seat state legislature drew a crowded field of 79 candidates. PH mounted the widest campaign by fielding 24 contenders, closely followed by BN with 23 candidates.
Newly formed outfit Parti Bersama Malaysia launched bids across 16 constituencies, while Bersatu and the Perikatan Nasional coalition contested seven and five seats respectively.
The Melaka showdown follows previous state polls in Johor and Negeri Sembilan where BN asserted its dominance, highlighting an awkward political reality where the two dominant coalitions clash as fierce rivals in state contests despite sharing power at the federal level in Putrajaya.
Political analysts view the election as a crucial bellwether for how the fragile BN-PH pact will hold up heading into the next general election.
The ballot box outcome will also provide the first tangible measure of public sentiment regarding the controversial transfer of former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak to house arrest. The court-sanctioned home detention order was executed just days before polling, dominating campaign rhetoric across the state and overshadowing localised municipal issues.

Title: Equal access to house arrest? That’s not Home Ministry’s call, says Saifuddin Nasution
Article:
LUMUT, Nov 14 — The Home Ministry acts solely as the implementing agency for the Pardons Board’s decisions on a prisoner’s sentence, including house arrest.
Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the ministry was not in a position to comment further on calls from various quarters regarding eligibility for house arrest, as pardon petitions fall outside its jurisdiction.
“So whether a pardon petition is discussed, considered and decided or not, that is not within the Home Ministry’s scope of responsibility.
“But if a decision is made, our job is to carry it out. Whether the sentence is reduced, set aside, or the person is released or placed under house arrest, our job is to implement it,” he told reporters.
He was speaking after launching the Madani Kita programme and the 2026 handover ceremony for the Malaysia Volunteers Department (RELA) Madani Adopted Village and Madani Adopted School at Kampung Sungai Tiram near here today.
Saifuddin Nasution was commenting on media reports about a recent statement by Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu that house arrest should not be a privilege reserved for certain groups, but should be considered fairly for all eligible prisoners.
On November 6, the Kuala Lumpur High Court allowed former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak, 73, to serve the remainder of his prison sentence in the SRC International Sdn Bhd case under house arrest at his residence in Langgak Duta, effective immediately until August 23, 2028.
Expanding on the legal perspective, Saifuddin Nasution said the right to submit a pardon petition is always open to any individual, regardless of status or background, once all judicial processes in court have been completed.
He said petitions submitted by prisoners while serving their sentences would be raised for the Pardons Board’s consideration at the federal level or before the Ruler or Sultan in their respective states.
“If there is a view that everyone should be given equal treatment, from a legal standpoint, that right already exists.
“As I said earlier, the first part is that anyone can apply. Whether the petition is entertained or not is another matter,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Melaka turnout hits EC’s 70pc target 50 minutes before polls close
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 14 — Voter turnout for the Melaka state election reached the 70 per cent targeted by the Election Commision (EC) by 5.10pm today, ahead of polls closing at 6pm.
EC real-time Voter Turnout Monitoring dashboard showed that 468,500 voters, or 70 per cent, had cast their ballots by then in the contest involving 79 candidates across 28 state seats.
Serkam continued to lead with a turnout of 79.08 per cent, followed by Ayer Molek at 78.57 per cent, Tanjung Bidara at 75.94 per cent and Sungai Rambai at 75.83 per cent shortly after 5pm.
Melaka’s rural and suburban seats have seen a positive voter turnout, with most reaching the 70 per cent mark as of 5pm.
However, Melaka’s key urban seats have registered lower voter turnout below the 66 per cent mark with Bandar Hilir at the bottom of the list with 57.55 per cent as of 5.30pm.
Bandar Hilir, a central Melaka seat, has recorded the lowest turnout among Melaka’s 28 state constituencies since polling started at 8am.
This is followed by Kota Laksamana at 62.62 per cent, Sungai Udang at 64.46 per cent, Ayer Keroh at 65.29 per cent and Kesidang at 65.64 per cent.
The Melaka state election has 79 candidates from various parties vying for 28 seats.
A total of 240 polling centres, comprising 1,213 polling streams, opened at 8am today for the 16th Melaka state election. Voting is scheduled to continue until 6pm.
Pakatan Harapan (PH) is fielding the highest number of candidates at 24, followed by Barisan Nasional (BN) with 23, Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) with 16, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (Bersatu) with seven, Perikatan Nasional (PN) with five, Parti Pribumi Perkasa Malaysia (Perkasa) with one and three independent candidates.
The election follows the dissolution of the 15th Melaka State Legislative Assembly on September 23, with the consent of Yang di-Pertua Negeri Tun Mohd Ali Rustam.
In the previous state election on November 20, 2021, BN won 21 of the 28 seats, while PH took five and PN secured two.

Title: Wedding day meets polling day as Melaka newlyweds cast votes in traditional red attire
Article:
ALOR GAJAH, Nov 14 — A newlywed couple made their wedding day even more memorable by taking time to cast their votes in the 16th Melaka state election today, arriving at the polling centre in their traditional red wedding attire.
Yau Wei Ming, 31, and his wife Chan Jia Lin, 27, headed to Sekolah Jenis Kebangsaan Cina (SJKC) Machap Baru here after their wedding ceremony at a temple.
The couple, from Kampung Machap Baru, caught the attention of fellow voters when they arrived in a specially hired classic car, accompanied by a convoy of several vehicles.
Yau Wei Ming, 31, and his wife Chan Jia Lin, 27, pose for a photograph after voting in the 16th Melaka state election at SJKC Machap Baru in Melaka, November 14, 2026. — Bernama pic
Yau said they had planned their wedding date a year ago but had not expected it to coincide with polling day.
“My wife has always liked traditional attire for our wedding. So, after completing our wedding ceremony today, we took the opportunity to cast our votes together.
“We feel proud and happy to be able to vote on such a special day,” he told reporters here today.
Yau, who works in the construction sector in Singapore, said they returned to Malaysia last Wednesday to prepare for their wedding and fulfil their responsibilities as voters.
He said he had voted three times previously, while this was his wife’s second time, adding that neither wanted to miss the opportunity despite their busy wedding schedule.
The Machap Jaya state seat is witnessing a three-cornered contest involving Pakatan Harapan candidate Datuk Ginie Lim Siew Lin, incumbent Datuk Ngwe Hee Sem of Barisan Nasional and Prasanth Kumar Brakasam of Parti Bersama Malaysia.
For the latest on the 16th Melaka state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/ — Bernama

Title: Seven impact marks, metal pellets found: Police probe suspected shooting at Sarikei business premises
Article:
SIBU, Nov 14 — Police are investigating a suspected shooting incident after a business premises’ metal shutter was found with seven impact marks along Jalan Repok, Sarikei.
Sarikei District Police Chief Supt Aswandy Anis said the premises owner lodged a report at 8.30pm on November 13 after hearing seven impact sounds coming from the direction of the shop’s folding metal shutter.
Upon checking outside, the complainant discovered seven marks believed to have been caused by gunfire on the shutter. No one was found at the scene.
Aswandy said preliminary investigations found two fragments of suspected metal pellets on the walkway outside the premises.
Further examination showed that the shutter had not been punctured, although its surface paint was damaged.
He said investigations were ongoing to determine the type of weapon used and identify those responsible.
No arrests have been made so far, while the motive remains under investigation.
The case is being investigated under Section 39 of the Arms Act 1960.
Members of the public with information on the incident are urged to contact investigating officer Insp Mohd Firza Ahmad Fauzi at 012-9768277 or visit the nearest police station.
Police also advised the public against spreading speculation that could affect public order, particularly in Sarikei. — The Borneo Post

Title: PM: Cyber, intrusion and terror threats top Malaysia’s security agenda as attacks hit thousands monthly
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Malaysia is currently facing thousands of cyber attack attempts every month, thereby demanding a faster and more robust level of preparedness from security forces in confronting new-millennium defence threats.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that the country’s security landscape is no longer focused solely on conventional military threats; instead, cyber attacks, system intrusions, and terrorist cell movements have become the most critical challenges today.
“We face thousands of attack attempts in a single month. Therefore, we must strengthen (our defence), and last week I met with the top leadership of the Malaysian Armed Forces (ATM) to discuss strengthening the cyber security unit within the Armed Forces,” he said.
He said this while answering a participant’s question during the “Temu Anwar” session with the National Young Heroes of the National Service Training Programme (PLKN 3.0) at the 515 Territorial Army Regiment Camp here, today.
To illustrate the seriousness of the threat, Anwar referred to a recent airport operational disruption incident in the United States (US), which stemmed from telecommunications system issues in that major superpower.
“Think about how the United States, with all its sophistication, could not identify the cause, but there was an attack on the telecommunication system that caused it to crash. We are still waiting for the final report,” he said.
Meanwhile, the Prime Minister emphasised that the pattern of national defence and asset procurement must rapidly adapt to the sophistication of modern technology, such as drone operations, without neglecting conventional defence aspects.
Recognising the urgent need to empower both dimensions of defence, Anwar, who is also the Minister of Finance, said that the government has elevated the Ministry of Defence’s allocation to the highest level in history, making it one of the largest recipient ministries alongside the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Health.
He said this substantial funding is crucial to replace various obsolete conventional assets of the security forces, including naval vessels, aircraft, and armoured vehicles.
“Because of obsolete aircraft and broken-down tanks, we are spending on all of that. However, regarding these procurements, the government also wants to ensure that past problems — such as the use of agents and high commissions that resulted in multi-million ringgit ship projects being abandoned — do not happen again,” he stressed. — Bernama

Title: Anwar says legacy debts like 1MDB pushed up Malaysia’s debt, cautions that corruption ruins nations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today sought to correct claims that Malaysia’s debts had increased under his management as finance minister.
He attributed the rise to debts inherited from previous governments, such as those linked to 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB).
Anwar said the federal government tries its best to fulfil the needs of all but has limited finances.
“Now, among big issues, they say Anwar manage the economy, the debt increases,” he said during a meet-up before over 200 female trainees at the National Service programme’s Camp 515 here, rejecting the claim.
Anwar said the government had steadily reduced its budget deficit since he became finance minister in 2022, cutting the gap between spending and revenue from about RM100 billion that year to around RM90 billion, RM80 billion and RM70 billion in the following years.
He noted that total debt still increased.
“It increased because have to pay old debts — 1MDB debt, Felda debt, I have to pay RM980 million per year; Tabung Haji debt, RM10 billion have to pay,” he said.
He added that the government sometimes also had to pay other debts, such as those for weapons procurement.
The federal government’s fiscal deficit has narrowed from 5.5 per cent of gross domestic product in 2022 to 3.7 per cent in 2025, and is projected to ease to 3.6 per cent this year and 3.3 per cent next year.
The gap between government expenditure and revenue fell from RM100.84 billion in 2022 to RM92.44 billion in 2023, RM80.9 billion in 2024 and RM76.6 billion in 2025, but is projected to rise to RM80.5 billion this year before easing to around RM79 billion next year.
Earlier at the same event, Anwar said some countries start out well or progress because of their unity, but later face problems such as corruption and arrogance.
He described negative attitudes towards corruption, such as those who think it would be “stupid” for those who become prime ministers not to use their position to garner riches.
He said such a culture would “
jahanam
” – meaning destroy – a country.

Title: Thunderstorms, strong winds to hit seven states, KL and Putrajaya until 6pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning for thunderstorms, heavy rain, and strong winds across seven states, as well as the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya, effective until 6pm today.
In a statement, MetMalaysia indicated that the adverse weather affects Penang and Kedah in Bandar Baharu, Kulim, Baling, Sik, Pendang, Kuala Muda, Yan, and Kota Setar.
In Perak, the affected areas include Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Perak Tengah, and Manjung.
A similar warning has been issued for Selangor, covering Klang, Kuala Langat, Sepang, Petaling, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, and Gombak as well as Negeri Sembilan in Port Dickson.
In Sabah, the warning covers the Interior division (Membakut), Tawau (Kalabakan), and the West Coast (Papar).
Meanwhile, in Sarawak, the affected areas are Miri (Marudi), Bintulu, Sibu (Selangau), Mukah (Dalat and Matu), Sri Aman (Pantu), and Limbang. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB confirms withdrawing letter to Rulers, maintains status quo of Tunku Muhriz
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 14 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has confirmed the withdrawal of the contents of a letter submitted to the Malay Rulers dated September 17 as well as the position previously taken by members of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (MMK) and effectively maintains the status quo regarding the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
He said the letter, which has circulated widely, was sent to the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal, Tan Sri Syed Danial Syed Ahmad, is self-explanatory.
“You have all read it, it has gone viral. The media has already commented extensively on it. So, I am confirming the letter. The letter is self-explanatory,” he told reporters after attending the Negeri Sembilan-level Deepavali Open House at the Seremban City Council (MBS) Hall here today.
Also present were the Undang of Luak Rembau, Datuk Sedia Raja Datuk Hassan Ab Hamid, and the Undang of Luak Jelebu, Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi.
Following this confirmation, Ismail expressed confidence that the impasse which has persisted in the state for the past few months is nearing settlement.
Earlier, a letter dated November 10 had circulated, concerning the withdrawal of the contents of a submission made to the Conference of Malay Rulers on September 17, as well as the position previously held by the members of the State Executive Council (MMK).
The letter states that Ismail, together with 10 members of the State Executive Council (Exco), has unanimously decided to retract the contents of a letter dated September 17.
This decision takes into account a media statement by the Malay Rulers dated October 14, as well as an order from the Seremban High Court dated June 5, which maintains the status quo regarding the position of the Yang Di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
The letter further explains that this decision was made to uphold the supremacy of the 1959 Negeri Sembilan State Constitution, preserve the order of the monarchical system, and ensure that the state administration continues to function in a peaceful and orderly manner.
“We reaffirm our commitment to always uphold our customs (
adat
) and to respect the position and authority of the royal institution within the state’s governance system.
“We also acknowledge the call by the Malay Rulers for any differences to be resolved through legitimate, authoritative, and credible channels, in a manner that is civil and consistent with our customs,” the letter reads.
The parties involved also expressed the view that efforts toward a resolution must be carried out with a strong sense of responsibility, in order to maintain harmony and stability in Negeri Sembilan and to prioritise the well-being of the people.
Meanwhile, Ismail could not provide further comment regarding the status of the 10 former Exco members, as he has not yet had the opportunity to have an audience with Tuanku Muhriz.
“As of now, since I have not yet had an audience with Tuanku, there is no further news. There have been no discussions regarding the status of the Exco members thus far. Once I have an audience [with His Highness], I will accept his views... for now, I cannot offer any comments,” he said.
The list of the 10 former Executive Council (Exco) members includes Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Datuk Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa, and Datuk Razali Abu Samah.
In another development, regarding the 2027 state budget, Ismail stated that he is still awaiting the consent of Tuanku Muhriz concerning the date for the legislative session.
“There is one point I must clarify to you all regarding the budget for the upcoming State Legislative Assembly session: the date I provided (November 26) is the date proposed by the state government.
“If His Highness consents to that date, we will proceed, it is entirely subject to his consent. The budget must be finalised before the end of the year,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Slowest seat in Melaka? A look at the Bandar Hilir vote
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 14 — Bandar Hilir recorded the lowest turnout among Melaka’s 28 state constituencies, at just under 56 per cent as of 4.30pm today.
The Election Commission’s (EC) real-time Voter Turnout Monitoring dashboard showed 67.78 per cent of ordinary voters statewide had cast their ballots, or 433,944 of 669,211 voters.
Serkam recorded the highest turnout at 74.09 per cent, putting it 20.72 percentage points ahead of Bandar Hilir.
Bandar Hilir has been occupying the bottom spot from the get-go when polling stations opened at 8am.
The seat has 23,042 registered voters, with women making up 52 per cent of voters and men 48 per cent.
Chinese voters make up about 73 per cent of the electorate, followed by Malays at 12.9 per cent, Indians at 6.4 per cent and others at 6.8 per cent.
It is a three-cornered fight between incumbent Leng Chau Yen of Pakatan Harapan (PH), Barisan Nasional (BN) candidate Jasmine Lok Huey Yee and Dr Mohd Nor Rashidi Ab Jalil of Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama).
Leng, of DAP, won the seat in 2021 with a majority of 7,778 votes in a four-cornered contest.
Turnout in the seat that year was 57.55 per cent, which today’s figure has yet to reach.
Lok, a Melaka Historic City Council councillor, is contesting for MCA, which was given the seat late in the day by BN.
The two women debated each other earlier during the campaign period when  Leng accepted an invitation from Lok.
Voting continues until 6pm today, so a late stage spurt could still change the numbers as the EC aims to hit a turnout target of 70 per cent overall.

Title: Melaka turnout closes in on 70pc target with over an hour of voting left
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 14 — Voter turnout in the Melaka state election reached 67.74 per cent as of 4.30pm today, approaching the Election Commission’s (EC) 70 per cent target with 90 minutes left before polling closes.
The EC’s real-time Voter Turnout Monitoring dashboard showed that 453,351 voters had cast their ballots in the contest involving 79 candidates across 28 state seats.

Title: Foreign minister: Malaysia urges Asean, China to redouble efforts to finalise South China Sea code
Article:
MANILA, Nov 14 — Malaysia has urged Asean and China to show renewed political will and step up efforts to finalise the draft South China Sea Code of Conduct (COC).
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the talks had intensified this year, with negotiations held monthly.
However, he said key issues, including the proposed code’s nature and geographical scope, remained unresolved and needed urgent attention.
He said Malaysia, which has co-chaired the negotiations since 2024, had worked closely with fellow Asean member states and China to steer the talks towards an effective and substantive COC within the three-year aspirational timeline agreed in 2023.
“I urge we redouble our collective efforts to finalise the draft COC as soon as possible. Renewed political will is imperative in achieving this goal, particularly at this final and critical stage,” he said in his intervention address at the Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting (AMM) here on Saturday.
Asean and China are aiming to conclude negotiations on the South China Sea COC by the end of 2026.
On Myanmar, Mohamad said the crisis remained one of the most pressing challenges to Asean’s unity and credibility.
He called for clear objectives and measurable progress in implementing the bloc’s Five-Point Consensus (5PC), which remains Asean’s main reference on Myanmar.
“We continue to emphasise, the need for clear objectives and measurable progress, particularly in the implementation of the 5PC,” he said.
He said Asean senior officials were discussing two proposals under a mandate from Asean leaders at the 48th Asean Summit in May.
The proposals are titled “The Non-Paper on the Terms of Reference of the proposed Special Envoy of Asean on Myanmar” and “The Non-Paper on Asean Elements to Assess Progress in Myanmar”. — Bernama

Title: National unity minister calls for year-round community bonding at national Deepavali celebration
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Open houses, social visits and neighbourly ties should be cultivated throughout the year, rather than only during festive seasons, said National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang.
He said such practices could strengthen bonds among Malaysia’s multiracial communities and ensure that diversity did not become a source of division.
“Unity must be reflected in our daily interactions, social concern and willingness to help one another. We must embrace the principles of understanding, respecting, accepting and celebrating diversity to build a progressive and harmonious society,” he said.
He was speaking at the 2026 national-level Deepavali celebration at Little India, Brickfields here today, officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Aaron said Malaysia’s strength and uniqueness as a multiracial nation lay not in the uniformity of its people, but in their ability to remain united despite their differences.
He said Malaysians shared a homeland, the Federal Constitution, the Rukun Negara and a common aspiration to develop the country and safeguard their collective interests, despite differences in religion, language, culture and traditions.
The event, organised by the Ministry of National Unity in collaboration with the Malaysian Associated Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (MAICCI), was also attended by Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh.
Themed “Cahaya Deepavali, Semarak Perpaduan”, the celebration featured Indian cultural and traditional performances, including Veenai and Mridangam classical music, Silambam, Kalaripayattu and Karra Samu martial arts, as well as a fashion show.
Visitors also had the opportunity to explore the Rumah KAMI (Ethnic House) booths, which showcased the heritage and traditions of the Malay, Chinese, Tamil, Telugu, Punjabi, Gujarati and Malayalee communities. — Bernama

Title: After nearly a decade, 647 Sri Pahang Flat residents closer to new homes, says Fahmi
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — A total of 647 out of 716 Sri Pahang Flat residents registered for the balloting process and offer of units at Residensi Maarof today, bringing them one step closer to owning new homes after nearly 10 years of waiting.
Lembah Pantai Member of Parliament Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the session, held at the Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) Training Institute, marked another important step before they moved into their new homes.
Fahmi, who is also Communications Minister, said he greatly appreciated the residents’ patience and cooperation throughout the redevelopment process.
“As the Lembah Pantai MP, I will continue to work with DBKL and all relevant parties to ensure that the welfare and interests of the residents remain a priority,” he said in a Facebook post.
Fahmi said Residensi Maarof was scheduled to be officially opened by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in the near future. — Bernama

Title: Women deserve equal chances to lead in security, defence, Anwar says, citing exam results
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said it would be unfair if women were not given equal opportunities to take on leadership roles.
Anwar noted that most personnel in the police and armed forces were men, citing the physically demanding nature of the work.
However, he acknowledged that women could also take on physically demanding duties.
“While we give space to women, there are also duties where there are many women, in education and medical. What we can focus now, in universities, more than 50 per cent are women, and now the results of examinations and tests, women outperform men, so it’s not fair if we don’t give them equal treatment,” he said during a question-and-answer session with female trainees at the National Service Training Programme 3.0 here.
A female trainee had asked Anwar what he considered the biggest challenge to be overcome in getting more women into leadership positions in the country’s security and defence sector.
During the brief exchange, the trainee also told Anwar that she is interested to join the Malaysian Army.
Anwar said he was proud of her confidence and quipped that young people should be confident because they were not doing anything wrong, such as stealing.
Anwar was speaking at the National Service Training Branch, Camp 515, Kuala Lumpur, attended in-person by 236 female trainees.
Another 1,663 trainees at seven other NS training camps joined the session via video conference.

Title: PM fulfils SK Polis Depot pupil’s invitation, attends school’s Anak Malaysia Carnival
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — The wish of a pupil of Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Polis Depot to invite Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to attend a programme at his school came true today when the country’s top leader took time to drop by the Anak Malaysia Carnival organised by the school.
Despite his hectic schedule, Anwar said he made the visit to fulfil the invitation from the pupil, identified as Muadz, while also taking the opportunity to personally inspect the school’s infrastructure and safety needs.
“Alhamdulillah, I was quite surprised to see how lively the carnival was — it was almost like a family day! It was heartening to see the children enthusiastically taking part in various activities, with some dressed as police personnel, soldiers and firefighters, while parents also joined in to enliven the school-organised carnival,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Anwar said during his visit to the school, located within the Police Training Centre (Pulapol) in Jalan Semarak, he also took time to hear directly from the headmaster about several matters requiring attention, particularly the condition of the school’s facilities and the comfort and safety of the pupils.
“Insya-Allah, I will look into the matters raised for further action,” he said.
The Prime Minister also expressed his appreciation to Muadz and the entire school community for the warm welcome, while urging the younger generation to remain enthusiastic about pursuing knowledge for the country’s future.
“I pray that you will succeed in achieving your ambitions and one day be able to contribute to society and the nation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: ‘We place so much hope in you’: Anwar urges NS trainees to shape Malaysia’s future
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today told National Service Training Programme 3.0 trainees that the country is placing great hope in them to secure Malaysia’s future.
As he ended his hour-long speech and dialogue session with the trainees, Anwar lowered his voice to deliver his closing message.
“This is my last word. We place so much hope – you cannot imagine – as an old man myself, struggle to make this country succeed and excel. You cannot imagine how much hope we have for you.
“You can ensure and give us that confidence that the future of this country, this great country, will be in good hands. When I see you, I believe, Insya Allah, Malaysia will be in good hands,” he said, drawing applause from the 200-odd trainees present.
Anwar was speaking during a meet-up at the National Service Training Branch, Camp 515 here where 236 female trainees were present in-person, while another 1,663 trainees at seven other training camps joined the session online via video conference.
He received a warm welcome from the trainees upon arrival, with four of them given the opportunity to ask him questions.
Earlier, National Service Training Department director-general Major-General Datuk Marzuki Mokhtar said in his welcoming speech that the programme is now in a new phase that is dynamic, progressive and relevant.
Beyond instilling discipline and promoting nation-building, Marzuki said the programme focused on three main areas: strengthening values, integrity and character; fostering unity across different races, religions and regions; and improving civic awareness and preparedness for modern challenges, including digital threats and public emergencies.
He said the aim was to develop a disciplined and patriotic younger generation with a strong sense of unity, critical thinking skills and readiness to contribute to the country and society.
He added that trainers were committed to conducting the programme with integrity, dedication and professionalism, while improving training quality and ensuring its safety and effectiveness.
“To us, the success of NS is not just measured by the number of trainees who completed training, but also the creation of a young generation that is patriotic, united and ready to serve the country,” he said.
Also present were Defence Ministry secretary-general Datuk Lokman Hakim Ali, the ministry’s deputy secretary-general (policy) Datuk Mohd Yani Daud, deputy secretary-general (management) Datin Roszanina Wahab, National Service Training Council chairman General (Rtd) Tan Sri Abdul Aziz Zainal, and Akademi Kenegaraan Malaysia director-general Datuk Roslan Hussin.

Title: ‘I want to survive as a Malaysian leader’: Anwar firm in not yielding to pressure for policies based on racial dominance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has asserted that he will not bow to pressure from certain quarters seeking to alter national policies to favour racial dominance, solely for the sake of political survival.
He said that the status of the Malay language as the national language, Islam as the religion of the Federation, and the special rights of the Malays and Bumiputeras are not matters to be disputed.
At the same time, he gave his assurance that he would remain committed to ensuring justice, well-being, and happiness for every citizen, regardless of their racial or religious background.
Anwar noted that although some have urged him to adjust national policies to prioritise racial dominance in order to maintain political power, he remains steadfast in his principle of leading Malaysia as a multi-ethnic nation.
“Nowadays, wherever I go, people tell me, ‘Anwar, you must adjust the policy, it must be Malay, Malay dominance. Otherwise, you won’t survive.’ My response is: I want to survive as a Malaysian leader who loves this country.”
“I want to uphold the principles of our nation and our Constitution,” he said while speaking at the National-Level Deepavali Celebration 2026 in Little India, Brickfields, today.
Also present were Minister of National Unity Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang, Minister of Communications Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh, and president of the Malaysian Associated Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (MAICCI) Datuk Seri N. Gobalakrishnan.
Meanwhile, the Prime Minister criticised certain quarters for using the issue of “racial survival” as a narrative for their cause, when in reality, they are alleged to be prioritising their own personal and family interests and wealth.
Anwar also rebuked a handful of associations and political parties for deliberately stoking racial sentiments to divert public attention away from issues of fraud and corruption.
“Look at the figures who talk about ‘racial survival.’ They are among the wealthiest people in our midst. Their ‘struggle’ is actually a pursuit to enrich themselves and their families,” he said.
In this regard, the Prime Minister urged all Malaysians to continue upholding the values of humanity, justice, and unity, the foundations of the nation’s strength in the spirit of Deepavali, which symbolises the triumph of light over darkness.
He noted that the message behind the festival is not only relevant to the Indian community but should be embraced by all citizens, regardless of their religion, race, or cultural background.
“Human beings must uphold virtuous values,” he said, referencing the teachings and philosophies of various religions, as well as the classic Tamil work Tirukkural, which emphasises moral principles, justice, humanity, and harmonious relations within society.
“Here (in Malaysia), we respect each other despite our differences, different religions, cultures, native languages, and ancestries yet we share a common humanity. We respect and appreciate one another. That is how Malaysia must be, how it must remain, and how it must succeed,” he said. — Bernama

Title: At national Deepavali event, Anwar says govt committed to addressing issues affecting Indian community
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 14 — The government remains committed to addressing issues affecting the Indian community in Malaysia, particularly those related to education and welfare, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said this included supporting the development of Tamil schools, promoting the Tamil language and improving the well-being of low-income Indians living in urban areas and estates.
Anwar said the government acknowledged that more needed to be done to effectively address the needs of the Indian community, particularly in education.
“We must also work to address and resolve issues involving Hindu temples, Indian traders and poor Indians living in urban areas and estates,” he said at the national-level Deepavali 2026 celebration in Little India, Brickfields here today.
The celebration, organised by the National Unity Ministry in collaboration with the Malaysian Associated Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (MAICCI), was also attended by National Unity Minister Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Human Resource Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh.
Meanwhile, Anwar stressed that the Madani Government’s approach was to ensure welfare assistance was distributed based on people’s actual needs, regardless of race, in line with efforts to ensure that all segments of society benefited from the country’s development.
He said this approach was reflected in initiatives such as Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), as well as the RM200 assistance provided to every school pupil in January, regardless of the type of school attended.
“We give every schoolchild RM200. Why? Because we care about their future,” he said.
He also urged Malaysians to uphold the spirit of togetherness, mutual respect and appreciation for the country’s religious, cultural, linguistic and ethnic diversity to preserve national harmony.
“Despite our differences in skin colour, religion, culture, language and ethnicity, we share a common humanity. We respect and value one another. That is how Malaysia must remain united and prosper as a nation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia proposes Sustainable Haze Fund, science diplomacy for transboundary haze fight at Asean meeting, says Tok Mat
Article:
MANILA, Nov 14 — Malaysia has called for a more proactive and coordinated Asean response to transboundary haze, advancing proposals for scientific cooperation and a Sustainable Haze Fund to strengthen the region’s preparedness.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said deteriorating air quality, including unhealthy and hazardous levels in several areas, posed serious risks to public health, livelihoods and daily activities, particularly among vulnerable populations.
“Moving forward, Asean must pursue a more proactive and coordinated regional response, anchored in the effective implementation of the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution.
“Complementing these efforts, Malaysia has advanced proposals on Science Diplomacy and a Sustainable Haze Fund, to strengthen scientific cooperation, sustainable financing, and collective response to transboundary haze pollution,” he said in his intervention at the Asean Foreign Ministers’ Meeting (AMM) here today.
Mohamad called for the ratification of the Asean Coordinating Centre for Transboundary Haze Pollution Control, saying its early deployment was essential to improving regional preparedness and responsiveness.
Mohamad expressed appreciation for Indonesia’s ongoing efforts to contain land and forest fires in Kalimantan and Sumatra that had severe transboundary haze in parts of the region.
He acknowledged the difficulties posed by the prevailing El Nino conditions, unpredictable weather, and the remoteness of affected areas.
“Malaysia would pursue its proposals at the Conference of the Parties to the Asean Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution in December, as well as through its chairmanship of the Ministerial Steering Committee on Transboundary Haze Pollution in 2027,” he said.
On broader regional cooperation, Mohamad also said that Asean needed to strengthen consensus and safeguard its centrality amid growing geopolitical and economic fragmentation, including increasingly complex cross-border security threats.
“United, Asean must continue to build and secure the region’s rules-based architecture, and remain as a voice of reason,” he said.
Mohamad emphasised that diversifying supply chains, deepening intra-Asean trade, and strengthening regional production networks remained paramount for the bloc’s resilience.
He said Malaysia welcomed the signing of the Asean Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) and looked forward to its implementation as a catalyst for digital connectivity, trade expansion and regional competitiveness.
On Asean-China relations, he also said the upcoming summit was expected to adopt joint statements marking the fifth anniversary of their Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and establishing an energy cooperation partnership, while noting China’s proposal to designate 2027 as the Asean-China Year of AI Cooperation.
Turning to Asean-Turkiye relations, Mohamad called for the timely conclusion of a comprehensive and forward-looking Plan of Action (POA).
“We must ensure the new POA delivers tangible outcomes, in areas of mutual interests, such as trade facilitation, supply chain resilience and defence industry cooperation,” he added. — Bernama
